svg.title: No-FFN docent model
svg.desc: The stages of the no-FFN docent: padded feature row, the hashed embedding table widened to 25 so the budget matches CD01, the pooled mean, and the two heads reading it directly; CD01's hidden layer is drawn crossed out; then the example query's intent probabilities and top-3 destinations.
svg.text: NO-FFN DOCENT -- features, pooled embedding, two heads, nothing between
WHAT: 26094 parameters (CD01: 26003); a query touches about 741 of them (its feature rows plus the heads).
example where is the cosmac demo
intent probabilities [navigate explain recommend story status unsupported] 1 0 0 0 0 0
Without the hidden layer the docent is a linear classifier over pooled hashed features.
WHY: sw-atlas bets its architecture on dropping feed-forward layers when knowledge comes from an external index; this is the
smallest honest check: the same features, corpus, heads, budget, and trainer as CD01, with only the FFN removed.
HOW: embed(1024, 25), linear(25, 6), linear(25, 13); loss = intent CE + destination CE; one adam step per row per epoch;
u:docent_logits_n and u:docent_loss_n in lib/docent.mlpl; the body is never constructed, so no unused parameter is counted.
The word-vector variant (SAN01b) does the same over CD01b's fine-tuned table; its width is fixed at 24 by the vectors.
LIMIT: a pooled bag of hashed features has no sequence mixing; it says nothing about attention-only encoders at Atlas size.
Held-out and paraphrase numbers are rows SAN01 and SAN01b in the docent results table and the comparison diagram, never here.
